title: Open Floor: Strategy & Risk Surface Review
summary: Leadership opened the floor to surface strategic risks and tradeoffs heading into FY27. Main threads: prioritizing Dedicated & Private go-to-market while preserving hosted velocity; tightening security/compliance cadence (SOC 2 Type II, ISO) and clearer on‑call/incident SLOs; careful hiring plan to extend runway; three immediate cross-functional experiments (canary rollouts, perf benchmarks, sales-led pilot). Next steps and owners captured at the end.

transcript:
HEADER:
Date: 2026-11-20
Start: 17:00 UTC
Duration: 72 minutes
Platform: Zoom (recorded)
Attendees: Priya Shah; Alex Nguyen; Diego Martinez; Samira Khan; ~120 employees (all-hands)
Links shared: FY27-strategy-draft.pdf (internal link), perf-bench-template.xlsx (internal link), SOC2-gap-list.docx (internal link)

AUTO SUMMARY (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
- Leadership framed FY27 priorities and asked teams to surface risk and blockers.
- Security & compliance cadence, hiring runway, and product packaging (dedicated vs private) were focal points.

TOP QUESTIONS (auto):
- How much can we push Dedicated without harming Hosted conversion?
- Do we need more headcount to hit service reliability SLAs?

ACTION ITEMS (captured live): see Action Items above

TRANSCRIPT BODY:
[00:00] Priya Shah: okay everyone um let's get started, thanks for coming on time we have a slightly different format today it's an open floor for strategy and risk surface uh please keep your questions concise, we'll try to ship clarity by the end
[00:18] Alex Nguyen: quick note, FY27 memo in the shared drive, the big trade-off we're asking teams to think about is velocity vs packaging; we can chase Dedicated & Private, both high-touch, but we need a plan that doesn't cannibalize hosted growth
[00:33] Speaker 3: (muffled) can you repeat the runway assumptions?
[00:37] Priya Shah: yeah, so high level — we assume current run rate plus 18 months of operations on current committed and cash, that informs our hiring cadence and capital allocation, if we accelerate Dedicated we'll need to be more selective on new hires
[00:52] Diego Martinez: on the eng side, the big risk I see is reliability under mixed workloads — long context chat sessions plus high QPS embedding spikes, we need stricter SLOs and an oncall flow that handles KV cache misses and cold-starts better
[01:08] Samira Khan: from security — SOC 2 Type II timeline is on track-ish but the dropout items are around vendor mapping and control evidence for Private deployments (VPC routing diagrams, KMS/HSM proof). We'll circulate a gap list after this meeting
[01:25] Speaker 5 (HR): two quick clarifications about hiring — no broad freeze is announced, but we're moving to a prioritization model, roles that directly unlock Dedicated & Private GTM will be privileged
[01:38] Priya Shah: that's right, prioritize revenue-impacting hires and critical platform roles; other reqs will need cross-functional approval
[01:44] [crosstalk] Someone: uh, pricing question — how are we thinking about Dedicated price floors?
[01:49] Alex Nguyen: good question, we want Dedicated to be predictable and margin-positive, experimental guardrails will keep a hosted fallback for price-sensitive customers; we'll run packaging experiments in Q1
[02:06] Speaker 7 (Engineering): Diego, can you expand on the perf benchmarks you mentioned? what representative workloads?
[02:12] Diego Martinez: yes, we'll pick four workloads — short-chat (8-32 tokens), long-chat (2k+ tokens), embedding batch (10k vectors), and rerank/LLM chain. We'll test fp16/quant and two kernel configs, publish the perf-bench-template.xlsx and an analysis
[02:30] Samira Khan: also need to ensure benchmark artifacts don't leak customer data; use synthetic traces and scrubbed logs
[02:37] Priya Shah: important — Samira, can you own the guardrails for benchmark data and a simple checklist for what can be shared?
[02:43] Samira Khan: yes, I'll add that to the SOC2 gap list and share
[02:47] [00:03:00] Speaker 9 (Sales): on the GTM side, customers ask for VPC and Private for regulated industries, but many just want data isolation and audit logs. Are we treating Private as a pure product motion or a compliance sales lever?
[03:10] Alex Nguyen: both — productize packaging to reduce bespoke work but keep a quick path for high-touch private installs; packaging experiments should measure seat economics and time-to-deploy
[03:25] Priya Shah: let's be explicit — Packaging Experiment A: 'Standard Dedicated' with 30-day deploy time, Packaging Experiment B: 'Private Lift' with 90-day deploy and premium pricing. We'll track conversions and operational cost per customer
[03:42] Speaker 12 (Finance): question about conversion lift vs cannibalization — if we make Dedicated too easy, will customers switch from hosted?
[03:51] Priya Shah: accepted, that's why experiments need control groups, we should have cohorts and AB tests. Diego, can infra tag traffic by cohort?
[03:59] Diego Martinez: yes, we can tag cohorts at routing layer, and instrument per-token cost in the console, but it requires minor runtime changes and an analytics schema update
[04:12] Speaker 14 (Support): ops question — incident playbook for model fallback isn't consistent across pods, we saw leakage last month where fallback didn't trigger correctly
[04:23] Diego Martinez: noted, we'll standardize a fallback playbook and a canary rollout flow. I'll own the technical runbook and Samira will sign off on security controls for the fallback
[04:35] Samira Khan: and we need audit logging for fallback events — who triggered it and why, that should be surfaced to customers in Private environments too
[04:45] [00:05:00] Priya Shah: pivoting briefly — hiring, I know teams want clarity; we'll publish a prioritized headcount plan 1) revenue/growth, 2) product & reliability, 3) long-term bets. No surprises but more discipline
[05:02] Speaker 18 (IC): with the prioritization, how does IC-level progression work? some folks worry promotions will slow
[05:12] Alex Nguyen: promotions continue, but resourcing for new roles will be more selective; managers should build business cases for each req
[05:21] Speaker 20 (Customer Ops): can we get a single source of truth for compliance docs? sales and CSMs keep sending old versions to customers
[05:29] Samira Khan: yes, I'll spin up a centralized folder and a short README with approved doc versions and a change log
[05:37] Speaker 22 (Product): product roadmap question — will we reprioritize mid-Q1 if Dedicated shows early traction?
[05:44] Priya Shah: yes, roadmap is dynamic; the FY27 memo has guardrails for pivot points and the conditions for reallocation
[05:50] Speaker 23 (IC): small thing — can we improve console token-cost visibility per route? customers keep asking for per-route cost breakdowns
[05:58] Alex Nguyen: on the roadmap backlog, cost-per-route is in the Optimize initiative; we'll try to accelerate the roll-out for the top 10 customers
[06:06] [00:10:00] Audience Q&A rapid-fire section (a few quick questions):
[10:08] Speaker 27: are we pursuing any M&A in the near term?
[10:12] Priya Shah: not public, we might look at tuck-ins that accelerate Dedicated or observability tech, but nothing concrete to share
[10:20] Speaker 30 (Engineer): any changes to open-source model support? we've had asks for new architectures and kernel patches
[10:27] Diego Martinez: continue to support new model families but prioritize those that align to serving runtime efficiency; community PRs that materially help latency will be prioritized
[10:34] Speaker 31 (Sales): on pricing — what's the timeline for pricing guardrails?
[10:38] Alex Nguyen: I'll propose guardrails in two weeks and a more formal packaging playbook by early December
[10:44] [00:40:00] (Mid-meeting recap) Priya Shah: quick recap, thank you — three experiments (perf benchmarks, packaging experiments, SOC2 gap closure), owners assigned, and we'll reconvene in two weeks with preliminary artifacts
[10:58] Speaker 33: small ask — more transparency on incident RCA outcomes; teams want learning not blame
[11:04] Diego Martinez: agree, we'll produce a short postmortem template with remediation and learning sections; will redact sensitive customer info
[11:12] Samira Khan: also proposing a monthly security bulletin summarizing control changes and audit outcomes
[11:18] [00:50:00] Final rounds, lightning updates from each leader:
[11:20] Priya Shah: org health is stable, focus on discipline and experiments
[11:26] Alex Nguyen: product: move packaging experiments to alpha by Jan and finalize metrics for success
[11:32] Diego Martinez: infra: canary flow and perf bench workstreams starting this week
[11:38] Samira Khan: security: gap list and doc control in the next 7 days
[11:44] [01:08:00] Closing: Priya Shah: thanks all, please fill out the feedback form, leaders will follow up with teams; we want speed with guardrails. End of meeting
